findings.evidence: Lines 5–43: `module`, imports, `public section`, `open Topology`, `variable ...`, then `theorem comap_pow_of_equiv` — no `namespace`. Line 23 reads `* \`Ideal.comap_pow_of_equiv\`: ...`. Line 39 is `omit [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] in`.
findings.fix: Wrap the lemma in `namespace Ideal ... end Ideal` so the name matches the docstring. Since it is pure ideal algebra (it needs `omit` of all four topological instances at line 39), it belongs in a non-topological file, e.g. `TauCeti/RingTheory/Ideal/`, rather than in a nonarchimedean-topology module that pure-algebra consumers must then import.
findings.issue: The module docstring (line 23) advertises `Ideal.comap_pow_of_equiv`, but the file has no `namespace` command, so the declared name is root-level `comap_pow_of_equiv`. The documented API name does not exist, and an unqualified `comap_pow_of_equiv` in the root namespace is far too generic for a lemma about `Ideal.comap`.

findings.evidence: The shadowing already bites inside the file: `_root_.PadicInt.maximalIdeal_eq_span_p` (lines 72, 99), `_root_.PadicInt.norm_le_pow_iff_mem_span_pow` (line 73), `_root_.PadicInt.isUnit_iff` (line 131). Roadmap `AdicSpaces/Suggested.lean:92,96` names these `isHuberRing_padicInt` / `not_isTateRing_padicInt`.
findings.fix: Put the two general p-adic facts in the root `PadicInt` namespace in a p-adic file (as with `IsAdic.comap`), and name the Huber results `TauCeti.Huber.isHuberRing_padicInt` / `TauCeti.Huber.not_isTateRing_padicInt` as the roadmap's `Suggested.lean` does, dropping the shadowing sub-namespace. This is separate from the still-open `PairOfDefinition.padicInt` naming question.
findings.issue: `namespace PadicInt` inside `TauCeti.Huber` creates `TauCeti.Huber.PadicInt`, shadowing Mathlib's root `PadicInt` for anyone who does `open TauCeti.Huber`, and it houses two declarations (`coe_maximalIdeal_pow_eq_setOf_norm_le`, `isAdic_maximalIdeal`) that mention no Huber notion but are reachable only by importing the whole Huber theory.

findings.evidence: The file itself writes `(p := p)` three times in its own statements (lines 107, 115, 116); `PairOfDefinition.discrete` at `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Basic.lean:237` takes `A` explicitly via `variable (A : Type*)` at line 234.
findings.fix: Make `p` explicit on the definition: `def PairOfDefinition.padicInt (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : PairOfDefinition ℤ_[p]`, matching the sibling `PairOfDefinition.discrete A`.
findings.issue: `PairOfDefinition.padicInt` takes `p` implicitly (from `variable {p : ℕ}` at line 63), but `p` appears only in the return type, so every mention outside an expected-type position must supply `(p := p)`.

summary: The new transport file documents `Ideal.comap_pow_of_equiv` but declares the lemma in the root namespace, and the p-adic file wraps general p-adic facts in a `TauCeti.Huber.PadicInt` namespace that shadows Mathlib's `PadicInt`. The pair of definition also takes `p` implicitly, forcing `(p := p)` at every mention.
